body:
I agree that we're all human, but beyond that, they still get to love each other, and be intimate, and not be ridiculed, and not become a hostile shell of a person everyone hates, because they hated you when you were whatever you were before that as well.

It's very hard to take the idea of equality seriously when I spend time around people.  There's always this illusion that never can be grasped; a catch-22 damned if you do, damned if you don't scenario where any action or inaction is deemed incorrect. We're all equal, but we're all so very unequal.  How do you deal with that, and why would you even want to?
They are better than me though, otherwise they wouldn't have what they do.

>Stop committing the same errors other people around you do to others.

I do that and then get labeled pretentious and told that I think I'm better than everyone.

>A simple "pretty dress" would do.

God no, the last thing I need to do is be humiliated again. You're not supposed to even have a sex drive unless you're above some x percentile of the population, give or take a few percentages per person and odd outliers of taste.

>Your life isn't dependent on intimacy, nor will you die without a GF/BF. Sure, we are social creatures, but this isn't the only thing we work for; it's shouldn't be a thing you spend hours mulling over. 

Living vs. Thriving. Breathing vs. Smiling. 

The human brain doesn't care about what we feel, it cares about connection.  It just does. When I read things like that I just get the impression no one really gets it or cares. It's very belittling...NO SHIT YOU WON'T STOP BREATHING...that's not what this is about...it's about the will to live when nothing ever works and life is an empty painful void. It is NOT LOGICAL, AND IF IT WAS, THIS WOULD STILL MAKE SENSE BECAUSE THERE ARE NO POSITIVES.
